report:
The process is paused at fact gathering. All three of A, B and C agreed not to sign papers until the will wording and money details are available, a lawyer explains the will, and an independent expert says what the house is worth. No discounted purchase is agreed.

The latest shared list has 35 brief entries and is in the latest list messages sent to A, B and C. C's final reply confirms that she has no new facts, does not object to fact gathering, and still does not agree to a discounted purchase. It does not change the list.

A and B will work together to gather the exact wording about the house, the name of the person handling Dad's will, any mortgage, debts, house value, or offer terms, a lawyer's explanation, and an independent valuer's view. They agreed to share the same documents with C and me. Because A and C are twins and B is younger, the lawyer should check any age wording and birth records. Because A hopes to buy, the lawyer and valuer should be independent.

A's wish to buy remains an option, B's need for money to start a dance studio remains on the list, and C's refusal remains on the list. Any discount would need the lawyer to confirm who must agree and written consent from everyone whose signature is needed. No sale terms, shares, or amounts were added. I have not made legal decisions or moved money.
